metadata.title: English Maze Chase Questions by CEFR Level
metadata.description: 36 rounds of 8 questions each. The player moves through a maze and eats the token with the correct answer while the ghosts chase. Topics, question difficulty and the number of options are calibrated to each CEFR level; the arcade difficulty (ghosts, speed and lives) is chosen by the player.
metadata.framework: CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages)

level_settings.options: How many answer tokens are placed in the maze (the extra ones are wrong answers).

question_fields.q: The prompt, with ___ for the gap.
question_fields.options: The FIRST option is the correct one. The game shuffles them and places one in each maze slot. Keep them short (up to about 12 characters) so they fit inside a token.
question_fields.explain: Short explanation shown after the answer is eaten.

A1.name: Beginner
A1.description: Everyday words and the first grammar rules: to be, to have, the simple present and time. Three answers in the maze.

puzzles.description: The verbs you use to talk about your day.

questions.q: I ___ breakfast at seven.
questions.explain: We have breakfast, lunch and dinner.

questions.q: She ___ to school by bus.
questions.explain: He, she and it add -s: she goes.

questions.q: They ___ football on Sundays.
questions.explain: We play football, tennis and games.

questions.q: He ___ a shower every morning.
questions.explain: We take a shower or have a shower.

questions.q: We ___ TV after dinner.
questions.explain: We watch TV and watch films.

questions.q: I ___ to music in the car.
questions.explain: We listen to music. Hear is not on purpose.

questions.q: My mother ___ dinner for us.
questions.explain: We cook dinner or make dinner.

questions.q: I ___ up at six o'clock.
questions.explain: Get up means to leave your bed.

puzzles.description: Am, is, are, have and has in short sentences.

questions.q: She ___ a doctor.
questions.explain: He, she and it take is.

questions.q: They ___ from Brazil.
questions.explain: We, you and they take are.

questions.q: I ___ twelve years old.
questions.explain: I always takes am.

questions.q: ___ you tired?
questions.explain: You takes are, in questions too.

questions.q: He ___ two brothers.
questions.explain: He, she and it take has.

questions.q: We ___ a big garden.
questions.explain: We, you and they take have.

questions.q: My sister ___ not at home.
questions.explain: One sister: is not (isn't).

questions.q: ___ they your friends?
questions.explain: They takes are.

puzzles.description: Rooms, furniture and things at home.

questions.q: We cook in the ___.
questions.explain: The kitchen is the room for cooking.

questions.q: I sleep in my ___.
questions.explain: A bed is in the bedroom.

questions.q: The car is in the ___.
questions.explain: We keep the car in the garage.

questions.q: We keep milk in the ___.
questions.explain: The fridge keeps food cold.

questions.q: Sit on the ___ and relax.
questions.explain: A sofa is for sitting in the living room.

questions.q: Open the ___, please. It's hot.
questions.explain: We open a window for fresh air.

questions.q: I take a shower in the ___.
questions.explain: The shower is in the bathroom.

questions.q: Go up the ___ to the first floor.
questions.explain: Stairs take you up and down.

puzzles.description: Food, drinks and words for eating.

questions.q: Coffee, tea and juice are ___.
questions.explain: We drink them, so they are drinks.

questions.q: An apple is a ___.
questions.explain: Apples, bananas and oranges are fruit.

questions.q: I eat ___ with butter for breakfast.
questions.explain: Bread and butter is a common breakfast.

questions.q: Carrots and tomatoes are ___.
questions.explain: They grow in a garden and are vegetables.

questions.q: We eat soup with a ___.
questions.explain: A spoon holds liquid food.

questions.q: A ___ of water, please.
questions.explain: We drink water from a glass.

questions.q: Chicken and beef are ___.
questions.explain: Meat comes from animals.

questions.q: Cake and ice cream are ___.
questions.explain: A dessert is the sweet food after a meal.

puzzles.description: Do, does and the -s ending for he, she and it.

questions.q: He ___ in a bank.
questions.explain: He, she and it add -s: he works.

questions.q: ___ she like pizza?
questions.explain: Questions with she use does + verb.

questions.q: They ___ not live here.
questions.explain: They use do not (don't) + verb.

questions.q: My dog ___ every night.
questions.explain: One dog: barks.

questions.q: We ___ English on Mondays.
questions.explain: We takes the verb with no -s.

questions.q: She ___ her homework after school.
questions.explain: We do homework, and she does it.

questions.q: ___ you speak Spanish?
questions.explain: You uses do + verb.

questions.q: The shop ___ at nine.
questions.explain: The shop is it, so it adds -s.

puzzles.description: Hours, days, months and numbers.

questions.q: The class starts ___ 8 o'clock.
questions.explain: We use at with clock times.

questions.q: My birthday is ___ June.
questions.explain: We use in with months and years.

questions.q: We have English ___ Monday.
questions.explain: We use on with days and dates.

questions.q: Ten plus five is ___.
questions.explain: 10 + 5 = 15, fifteen.

questions.q: The day after Monday is ___.
questions.explain: The week goes Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.

questions.q: It's 7:30. It's half ___ seven.
questions.explain: Half past seven means 7:30.

questions.q: December is the ___ month.
questions.explain: December is number 12 of the year.

questions.q: There are ___ days in a week.
questions.explain: A week has seven days.

A2.name: Elementary
A2.description: The past, plans, comparisons and travel vocabulary. Three answers in the maze.

puzzles.description: The past forms that don't end in -ed.

questions.q: I ___ to Rio last year.
questions.explain: The past of go is went.

questions.q: She ___ a new phone yesterday.
questions.explain: The past of buy is bought.

questions.q: We ___ pizza for dinner.
questions.explain: The past of eat is ate.

questions.q: He ___ me the truth.
questions.explain: The past of tell is told.

questions.q: They ___ home at midnight.
questions.explain: The past of come is came.

questions.q: I ___ my keys this morning.
questions.explain: The past of lose is lost.

questions.q: The film ___ at nine.
questions.explain: The past of begin is began.

questions.q: She ___ very well last night.
questions.explain: The past of sleep is slept.

puzzles.description: Airports, hotels and words for a trip.

questions.q: We stayed in a cheap ___.
questions.explain: You sleep in a hotel when you travel.

questions.q: Show your ___ at the airport.
questions.explain: A passport is your travel document.

questions.q: Our ___ leaves at 6 a.m.
questions.explain: A flight is a journey by plane.

questions.q: I packed my ___ last night.
questions.explain: You pack clothes in a suitcase.

questions.q: We ___ a car for the weekend.
questions.explain: You rent a car and give it back later.

questions.q: The hotel is ___ the beach.
questions.explain: Near means close to.

questions.q: We took lots of ___ on the trip.
questions.explain: You take photos with a camera or phone.

questions.q: I need to ___ a room for two nights.
questions.explain: Book means to reserve in advance.

puzzles.description: Buying clothes, sizes and prices.

questions.q: Can I ___ these jeans on?
questions.explain: Try on means to test clothes in the shop.

questions.q: How much ___ these shoes cost?
questions.explain: Shoes is plural, so we use do.

questions.q: The T-shirt is on ___: 50% off!
questions.explain: On sale means with a lower price.

questions.q: What ___ do you wear?
questions.explain: Clothes come in sizes: S, M, L.

questions.q: It's cold. Put on your ___.
questions.explain: A coat keeps you warm.

questions.q: These shoes don't ___ me: they're too big.
questions.explain: Fit is about the size being right.

questions.q: Keep the ___ if you want to return it.
questions.explain: A receipt is the paper proving you paid.

questions.q: Can I ___ this shirt for a bigger one?
questions.explain: Exchange means to swap for another item.

puzzles.description: Bigger, the biggest, as ... as.

questions.q: This book is ___ than that one.
questions.explain: The comparative of good is better.

questions.q: She is the ___ student in the class.
questions.explain: The superlative of good is the best.

questions.q: Today is ___ than yesterday.
questions.explain: Short adjectives double the last letter: hotter.

questions.q: My car is ___ expensive than yours.
questions.explain: Less + adjective + than is the opposite of more.

questions.q: He runs ___ than me.
questions.explain: Short words add -er: faster.

questions.q: It's the ___ film I've ever seen.
questions.explain: The superlative of bad is the worst.

questions.q: Anna is as tall ___ her brother.
questions.explain: The structure is as + adjective + as.

questions.q: This is the ___ interesting book here.
questions.explain: Long adjectives take the most.

puzzles.description: Plans, predictions and decisions.

questions.q: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.explain: We use going to when we can see the evidence.

questions.q: I think she ___ pass the exam.
questions.explain: After I think we normally use will.

questions.q: We ___ visit my aunt: the tickets are booked.
questions.explain: A decision already made takes going to.

questions.q: Don't worry, I ___ help you.
questions.explain: An offer made now takes will.

questions.q: ___ you be at home tonight?
questions.explain: Questions about the future use will.

questions.q: They ___ get married in June.
questions.explain: Be + going to + verb: they are going to get married.

questions.q: It's cold in here. I ___ close the window.
questions.explain: A decision made at that moment takes will.

questions.q: I've decided: I ___ study medicine.
questions.explain: A plan you have decided takes going to.

puzzles.description: In, on, at, across, through and more.

questions.q: Walk ___ the bridge to cross the river.
questions.explain: Across means from one side to the other.

questions.q: The bank is ___ the café and the shop.
questions.explain: Between is used with two things.

questions.q: She walked ___ the forest.
questions.explain: Through is used inside something, like a forest.

questions.q: The plane flew ___ the city.
questions.explain: Over means above and across.

questions.q: Put the milk ___ the fridge.
questions.explain: In is used for the inside of something.

questions.q: We arrived ___ the airport at six.
questions.explain: We arrive at a place and arrive in a city.

questions.q: He ran ___ the stairs to the roof.
questions.explain: Up shows movement to a higher place.

questions.q: The museum is ___ the corner.
questions.explain: Around the corner means very close.

B1.name: Intermediate
B1.description: Present perfect, conditionals, phrasal verbs and vocabulary for work and health. Three answers in the maze.

puzzles.description: Experiences, results and for, since and yet.

questions.q: I ___ never been to Japan.
questions.explain: I, you, we and they take have.

questions.q: She ___ worked here since 2019.
questions.explain: He, she and it take has.

questions.q: ___ you finished your report yet?
questions.explain: Yet goes with the present perfect.

questions.q: We've lived here ___ ten years.
questions.explain: For + a period of time: for ten years.

questions.q: He's just ___ the news.
questions.explain: After have we use the past participle.

questions.q: I haven't seen her ___ Monday.
questions.explain: Since + a point in time: since Monday.

questions.q: They ___ already left.
questions.explain: Already goes between have and the participle.

questions.q: How long ___ you known him?
questions.explain: How long + present perfect for something still true.

puzzles.description: Jobs, salaries and spending.

questions.q: I'm going to ___ for the job online.
questions.explain: You apply for a job.

questions.q: He has a job ___ tomorrow.
questions.explain: A job interview is the talk before being hired.

questions.q: We're short of money. We need to ___.
questions.explain: Save means to keep money for later.

questions.q: I get ___ at the end of the month.
questions.explain: Get paid means to receive your salary.

questions.q: The company ___ 200 people.
questions.explain: A company employs its workers.

questions.q: I work ___ time: 40 hours a week.
questions.explain: Full time is the opposite of part time.

questions.q: She got a ___ and now earns more.
questions.explain: A raise (or rise) is more money in your salary.

questions.q: Can I pay by ___?
questions.explain: We say pay by card but pay in cash.

puzzles.description: Two-word verbs you hear every day.

questions.q: I ___ up at six every day.
questions.explain: Get up means to leave your bed.

questions.q: Please ___ off your shoes.
questions.explain: Take off is the opposite of put on.

questions.q: Can you ___ up the music? I can't hear it.
questions.explain: Turn up means to make louder.

questions.q: She ___ after her little brother.
questions.explain: Look after means to take care of.

questions.q: We've ___ out of coffee.
questions.explain: Run out of means to have none left.

questions.q: He ___ up smoking last year.
questions.explain: Give up means to stop a habit.

questions.q: Don't ___ up! You can do it.
questions.explain: Give up also means to stop trying.

questions.q: The plane ___ off on time.
questions.explain: Take off is what a plane does when it leaves.

puzzles.description: Symptoms, doctors and staying healthy.

questions.q: I have a ___ throat.
questions.explain: A sore throat hurts when you swallow.

questions.q: The doctor gave me a ___ for antibiotics.
questions.explain: A prescription lets you buy medicine.

questions.q: My head hurts. I have a ___.
questions.explain: Ache + the part of the body: headache.

questions.q: You should see a ___ about that tooth.
questions.explain: A dentist treats teeth.

questions.q: He ___ his leg skiing.
questions.explain: The past of break is broke.

questions.q: Eat well and ___ regularly to stay healthy.
questions.explain: After and we repeat the same verb form: eat ... exercise.

questions.q: I feel ___. I think I'll go to bed.
questions.explain: Feel + adjective: feel ill.

questions.q: She's ___ to peanuts.
questions.explain: Be allergic to something.

puzzles.description: Zero, first and second conditionals.

questions.q: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll stay home.
questions.explain: After if we use the present, not will.

questions.q: If I ___ rich, I'd travel the world.
questions.explain: Second conditional: if + past (were).

questions.q: Water boils if you ___ it to 100°C.
questions.explain: Zero conditional: present in both parts.

questions.q: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.explain: General facts take the present in both parts.

questions.q: I would call her if I ___ her number.
questions.explain: Second conditional: would + if + past.

questions.q: If you ___ harder, you'll pass.
questions.explain: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

questions.q: What would you do if you ___ the lottery?
questions.explain: An imaginary situation takes the past form.

questions.q: If I were you, I ___ accept the job.
questions.explain: If I were you + would is how we give advice.

puzzles.description: Turning verbs and nouns into adjectives and adverbs.

questions.q: Be ___ with that glass!
questions.explain: Care + ful makes the adjective careful.

questions.q: This job is very ___.
questions.explain: A thing is stressful; a person feels stressed.

questions.q: I was ___ by the film.
questions.explain: -ed describes how you feel; -ing describes the thing.

questions.q: The instructions were so ___ that nobody understood.
questions.explain: Un- makes the opposite: unclear.

questions.q: He works as a ___.
questions.explain: -ian and -er often make the person: musician.

questions.q: There's a lot of ___ in this city.
questions.explain: -tion makes the noun: pollution.

questions.q: She spoke ___ about her country.
questions.explain: -ly makes the adverb: proudly.

questions.q: We need a ___ to this problem.
questions.explain: The noun of solve is solution.

B2.name: Upper Intermediate
B2.description: Collocations, deduction, reported speech and linking words, with four answers in the maze.

puzzles.description: The verbs that go with each noun.

questions.q: Could you ___ me a favour?
questions.explain: We do someone a favour.

questions.q: I need to ___ a decision today.
questions.explain: We make a decision in English, not take one.

questions.q: She ___ a lot of progress this year.
questions.explain: Make progress is a fixed collocation.

questions.q: Let's ___ a break.
questions.explain: We take a break (or have a break).

questions.q: He ___ his best to help.
questions.explain: Do your best is fixed.

questions.q: Don't ___ a risk like that.
questions.explain: We take risks.

questions.q: They have ___ business with us for years.
questions.explain: Do business with someone.

questions.q: I'd like to ___ a complaint.
questions.explain: We make a complaint.

puzzles.description: Must, can't, might and could for guessing.

questions.q: She isn't answering. She ___ be asleep.
questions.explain: Must be shows you are almost certain.

questions.q: That ___ be John: he's in Canada.
questions.explain: Can't be is the opposite of must be.

questions.q: They ___ have left: the lights are off.
questions.explain: Must have + participle for a past deduction.

questions.q: He ___ be at home, but I'm not sure.
questions.explain: Might shows a possibility.

questions.q: You ___ have seen her: she wasn't there.
questions.explain: Can't have + participle means it was impossible.

questions.q: It ___ have been raining: the ground is wet.
questions.explain: The evidence makes you almost certain.

questions.q: I'm not sure, but they ___ know the answer.
questions.explain: May is like might: a possibility.

questions.q: He ___ have forgotten the meeting.
questions.explain: Could have + participle shows a past possibility.

puzzles.description: Energy, waste, data and devices.

questions.q: Glass bottles can be ___ and used again.
questions.explain: Recycle means to turn waste into new products.

questions.q: Solar and wind are ___ sources of energy.
questions.explain: Renewable energy never runs out.

questions.q: The company wants to cut its carbon ___.
questions.explain: Carbon footprint is the CO2 you produce.

questions.q: My phone ___ out of battery.
questions.explain: Run out of means to finish the supply.

questions.q: Please ___ the app before using it.
questions.explain: Download brings a file to your device.

questions.q: The files are stored in the ___.
questions.explain: The cloud means storage on remote servers.

questions.q: Cutting down forests causes ___.
questions.explain: Deforestation is the loss of forests.

questions.q: Turn off the lights to ___ energy.
questions.explain: Save energy means to use less of it.

puzzles.description: Telling people what someone else said.

questions.q: He said he ___ tired.
questions.explain: Present becomes past in reported speech.

questions.q: She told me she ___ the film before.
questions.explain: Present perfect becomes past perfect.

questions.q: They asked me where I ___.
questions.explain: Reported questions use normal word order.

questions.q: He said he ___ call me the next day.
questions.explain: Will becomes would.

questions.q: She asked me if I ___ help her.
questions.explain: Can becomes could.

questions.q: Mark said he ___ finished his homework.
questions.explain: Have finished becomes had finished.

questions.q: The teacher told us ___ quiet.
questions.explain: Tell someone to + verb reports an order.

questions.q: He asked what time the film ___.
questions.explain: The tense moves back and the order stays normal.

puzzles.description: Words that look alike but behave differently.

questions.q: The news didn't ___ me at all.
questions.explain: Affect is the verb; effect is usually the noun.

questions.q: Could you ___ me your pen?
questions.explain: You lend something to someone; you borrow from them.

questions.q: The number of students has ___.
questions.explain: Rise has no object; raise needs one.

questions.q: We ___ him to be honest with us.
questions.explain: Expect someone to do something.

questions.q: He works as an ___ in a bank.
questions.explain: The person is an economist.

questions.q: I'm ___ forward to the weekend.
questions.explain: Look forward to something good.

questions.q: Do you mind if I ___ your phone for a second?
questions.explain: Use is the neutral verb here.

questions.q: She has a great ___ of humour.
questions.explain: Sense of humour is a fixed phrase.

puzzles.description: Contrast, reason, result and condition.

questions.q: ___ the rain, we went for a walk.
questions.explain: Despite + noun; although + clause.

questions.q: He was tired; ___, he finished the race.
questions.explain: However introduces a contrasting sentence.

questions.q: ___ she was ill, she went to work.
questions.explain: Although + subject + verb.

questions.q: We were late ___ the traffic.
questions.explain: Because of + noun; because + clause.

questions.q: Take an umbrella ___ it rains.
questions.explain: In case means as a precaution.

questions.q: I'll help you ___ you ask nicely.
questions.explain: As long as sets a condition.

questions.q: She studied hard; ___, she passed.
questions.explain: Therefore introduces a result.

questions.q: ___ you hurry, you'll miss the train.
questions.explain: Unless means if ... not.

C1.name: Advanced
C1.description: Idioms, precise adjectives, inversion and the prepositions that follow each word. Four answers in the maze.

puzzles.description: Expressions native speakers use all the time.

questions.q: The project is on the back ___ for now.
questions.explain: On the back burner means postponed.

questions.q: Let's call it a ___ and go home.
questions.explain: Call it a day means to stop working.

questions.q: She let the cat out of the ___.
questions.explain: Let the cat out of the bag means to reveal a secret.

questions.q: Don't worry, it's not rocket ___.
questions.explain: Not rocket science means not complicated.

questions.q: He's on the ___ about the offer.
questions.explain: On the fence means undecided.

questions.q: That was the last ___.
questions.explain: The last straw is the final problem you can accept.

questions.q: Stop beating around the ___.
questions.explain: Beat around the bush means to avoid the subject.

questions.q: The repairs cost an arm and a ___.
questions.explain: Cost an arm and a leg means to be very expensive.

puzzles.description: The verb each noun expects.

questions.q: The company is ___ a loss this year.
questions.explain: Make a loss, make a profit.

questions.q: She ___ a strong case for the change.
questions.explain: Make a case means to argue for something.

questions.q: They ___ serious concerns about the plan.
questions.explain: Raise concerns, raise a question.

questions.q: He ___ the blame for the mistake.
questions.explain: Take the blame means to accept responsibility.

questions.q: Let me ___ your attention to page four.
questions.explain: Draw someone's attention to something.

questions.q: The results ___ our expectations.
questions.explain: Exceed expectations means to be better than expected.

questions.q: We need to ___ a compromise.
questions.explain: Reach a compromise or an agreement.

questions.q: They ___ to a conclusion after hours of debate.
questions.explain: Come to a conclusion (or reach a conclusion, with no to).

puzzles.description: Putting the auxiliary first for effect.

questions.q: Never ___ I seen such a beautiful sunset.
questions.explain: After never, the auxiliary comes before the subject.

questions.q: Not only ___ he late, he also forgot the tickets.
questions.explain: Not only + inverted auxiliary: not only was he late.

questions.q: Hardly ___ I arrived when the phone rang.
questions.explain: Hardly had I ... when is a fixed pattern.

questions.q: Only after the meeting ___ we learn the truth.
questions.explain: Only after + inversion in the main clause.

questions.q: It ___ John who broke the window.
questions.explain: A cleft sentence: it was John who ...

questions.q: ___ I known, I would have helped.
questions.explain: Had I known replaces if I had known.

questions.q: Under no circumstances should ___ the door.
questions.explain: After the inverted auxiliary, the subject and the base verb follow.

questions.q: So loud ___ the music that we left.
questions.explain: So + adjective + was/were + subject.

puzzles.description: The preposition that belongs to each word.

questions.q: She's very good ___ solving problems.
questions.explain: Good at + noun or -ing.

questions.q: He's responsible ___ the whole team.
questions.explain: Responsible for something or someone.

questions.q: I'm not familiar ___ that software.
questions.explain: Familiar with something.

questions.q: They accused him ___ lying.
questions.explain: Accuse someone of something.

questions.q: Everything depends ___ the weather.
questions.explain: Depend on something.

questions.q: She apologised ___ being late.
questions.explain: Apologise to a person for an action.

questions.q: We're fully aware ___ the risks.
questions.explain: Aware of something.

questions.q: He insisted ___ paying for dinner.
questions.explain: Insist on + noun or -ing.

puzzles.description: Choosing the adjective that says exactly what you mean.

questions.q: After the marathon, she was absolutely ___.
questions.explain: Exhausted is an extreme adjective: very tired.

questions.q: The view from the top was ___.
questions.explain: Breathtaking means extremely beautiful.

questions.q: His answer was ___: nobody knew what he meant.
questions.explain: Ambiguous means open to more than one meaning.

questions.q: She gave a ___ account, with every detail.
questions.explain: Thorough means complete and careful.

questions.q: The evidence was ___: there was no doubt.
questions.explain: Conclusive evidence settles the question.

questions.q: He made a ___ remark that offended everyone.
questions.explain: Tactless means without care for other people's feelings.

questions.q: The instructions were ___ and easy to follow.
questions.explain: Concise means short and clear.

questions.q: It was a ___ decision, made without thinking.
questions.explain: A rash decision is taken too quickly.

puzzles.description: The verbs of reports, studies and essays.

questions.q: The study ___ a link between sleep and memory.
questions.explain: Research suggests, shows or indicates something.

questions.q: The author ___ that the policy failed.
questions.explain: Argue that + clause is standard in academic writing.

questions.q: Researchers ___ data from 30 countries.
questions.explain: The past of the verb analyse is analysed.

questions.q: These findings ___ previous research.
questions.explain: One result contradicts another.

questions.q: The graph ___ a steady increase.
questions.explain: Charts illustrate, show or demonstrate.

questions.q: We need to ___ the results carefully.
questions.explain: Interpret means to explain what data means.

questions.q: The theory ___ on three assumptions.
questions.explain: A theory rests on (is based on) its assumptions.

questions.q: The final section ___ the main arguments.
questions.explain: Summarise means to give the main points.

C2.name: Proficiency
C2.description: Fine differences in meaning, idiomatic language, register and the structures of formal English. Four answers in the maze.

puzzles.description: Words that are close in meaning but not interchangeable.

questions.q: The talk was ___: an hour with no clear point.
questions.explain: Rambling means long and disorganised.

questions.q: Her review of the novel was ___ but fair.
questions.explain: Scathing means severely critical.

questions.q: He gave a ___ apology that convinced nobody.
questions.explain: Perfunctory means done without real interest.

questions.q: The evidence for the theory is ___ at best.
questions.explain: Tenuous means weak or very slight.

questions.q: She has a ___ memory for names.
questions.explain: Prodigious means impressively large.

questions.q: The changes were ___, barely noticeable.
questions.explain: Imperceptible means too small to notice.

questions.q: His argument was ___ and hard to refute.
questions.explain: Cogent means clear and convincing.

questions.q: After ten hours, the talks reached an ___.
questions.explain: An impasse is a deadlock, with no way forward.

puzzles.description: Fixed expressions that don't translate word for word.

questions.q: The new rule is a ___ in the ointment.
questions.explain: A fly in the ointment is a small thing that spoils something.

questions.q: He was given a ___ hand to redesign the site.
questions.explain: A free hand means complete freedom to decide.

questions.q: They decided to bite the ___ and tell the truth.
questions.explain: Bite the bullet means to face something unpleasant.

questions.q: The deal fell ___ at the last minute.
questions.explain: Fall through means to fail before it is completed.

questions.q: That story sounds odd: take it with a pinch of ___.
questions.explain: Take it with a pinch of salt means don't fully believe it.

questions.q: All that paperwork is a ___ in the neck.
questions.explain: A pain in the neck is something annoying.

questions.q: We have no plan; let's play it by ___.
questions.explain: Play it by ear means to improvise.

questions.q: After a terrible year, the company is in the ___.
questions.explain: In the red means losing money.

puzzles.description: The formal word for an everyday one.

questions.q: Formal for 'ask for': to ___.
questions.explain: Request is the formal verb.

questions.q: Formal for 'find out': to ___.
questions.explain: Ascertain means to establish with certainty.

questions.q: Formal for 'help': to ___.
questions.explain: Assist is the formal equivalent.

questions.q: Formal for 'about' (a subject): ___.
questions.explain: Regarding or concerning introduces the topic.

questions.q: Formal for 'enough': ___.
questions.explain: Sufficient is the neutral formal word.

questions.q: Formal for 'buy': to ___.
questions.explain: Purchase appears in contracts and receipts.

questions.q: In a formal letter: we ___ receipt of your application.
questions.explain: Acknowledge receipt is a fixed formal phrase.

questions.q: Formal for 'start' (a process): to ___.
questions.explain: Commence is the formal verb; the others are informal.

puzzles.description: Subjunctive, inversion and emphatic patterns.

questions.q: ___ it not been for her, we would have failed.
questions.explain: Had it not been for replaces if it had not been for.

questions.q: I insist that he ___ present at the meeting.
questions.explain: After insist that, the subjunctive uses the base form.

questions.q: ___ he to resign, the team would collapse.
questions.explain: Were + subject + to is a formal conditional.

questions.q: So ___ was the evidence that the case collapsed.
questions.explain: So + adjective + was + subject is emphatic inversion.

questions.q: It is essential that every student ___ on time.
questions.explain: It is essential that + base form (subjunctive).

questions.q: Little ___ that the deal had already failed.
questions.explain: Little + auxiliary + subject is an inverted structure.

questions.q: No sooner ___ than the rain started.
questions.explain: No sooner had ... than is a fixed pattern.

questions.q: Such ___ his anger that he left the room.
questions.explain: Such + was + subject, agreeing with anger (singular).

puzzles.description: Phrasal verbs in the news and at work.

questions.q: The government has ___ back on spending.
questions.explain: Cut back on means to reduce.

questions.q: We need to ___ up with a better plan.
questions.explain: Come up with means to produce an idea.

questions.q: Police are ___ down on speeding.
questions.explain: Crack down on means to act firmly against.

questions.q: She ___ through a difficult period last year.
questions.explain: Go through means to experience something hard.

questions.q: He finally ___ up to his mistake.
questions.explain: Own up to means to admit.

questions.q: The talks ___ down over pay.
questions.explain: Break down means to fail or collapse.

questions.q: I can't ___ up with this noise any longer.
questions.explain: Put up with means to tolerate.

questions.q: They ___ off the meeting until Friday.
questions.explain: Put off means to postpone; call off means to cancel.

puzzles.description: The words that organise an argument.

questions.q: ___, the results were disappointing.
questions.explain: All in all introduces a summary.

questions.q: The plan is expensive; ___, it may be worth it.
questions.explain: That said introduces a contrasting point.

questions.q: ___, the report ignores the main issue.
questions.explain: Crucially marks the most important point.

questions.q: We have two options, ___ selling or renting.
questions.explain: Namely introduces the specific items.

questions.q: ___ speaking, the data supports the theory.
questions.explain: Broadly speaking means in general terms.

questions.q: He arrived late; ___, he missed the opening.
questions.explain: Consequently introduces a result.

questions.q: ___, let us consider the costs.
questions.explain: Firstly opens a list of points.

questions.q: The price is high; ___, demand keeps growing.
questions.explain: Nonetheless signals a contrast; the others signal a result.
